evals.name: velocity-reservation-unknown-duration
evals.prompt: The reservation intent for VeloCity got accepted in yesterday's product meeting. Can you write the spec for it so we can go through it with the domain expert on Thursday?
evals.expected_output: docs/specs/rider-reserves-bike-at-station.md with 3-6 rules (reserve available bike, one active reservation per rider, reserved bike blocked for others incl. rental, expiry), concrete GWT examples with IDs, contract with Reserve Bike command and both outcome events (Bike Reserved, Reservation Expired), reservation duration left as '?' + open question, no bounded contexts/endpoints, intent stays 'accepted' (not approved by the skill), report lists open questions.
assertions: Spec file at docs/specs/rider-reserves-bike-at-station.md (1:1 with the intent name)
Rules are illustrated by at least 3 Given/When/Then examples
Examples use concrete values (named actors, identifiers or numbers)
No solution vocabulary outside a technical-notes section
Every business-outcome event of the intent appears in the spec
Spec stays lean (at most 1500 words)
Contract lists commands and events in domain language
Spec passes specs.py check (0 errors)
No plan, canvas, context map or code produced
Reservation duration not invented (no concrete duration outside open questions)
Reservation duration recorded as an open question
Spec states that a reserved bike can't be rented by another rider (agrees with the rent intent)
Intent left 'accepted' (the spec was not self-approved)
Final message lists open questions for the domain expert

evals.name: draft-intent-gate

evals.expected_output: No spec file; explains the intent rider-reports-faulty-bike is still a draft and must be reviewed/accepted first; does not change the intent's status on its own.
assertions: No spec file created for a draft intent

Intent status unchanged (still draft)

evals.name: answer-questions-and-approve
evals.prompt: Domain expert answers for the reservation spec: Q1 - a reservation lasts 15 minutes. Q2 - the rider must take exactly the bike they reserved. Everything else looks right, so the spec is approved.
evals.expected_output: Spec updated: '?' replaced with 15 minutes in examples/data (e.g. 10:00 -> 10:15 boundary), Q1/Q2 removed from open questions, possibly an example for Q2 (Anna can't rent another bike instead / reserved bike only by Anna); specs.py approve run: spec status approved, intent status specified; intents README rebuilt.
assertions: Spec file at docs/specs/rider-reserves-bike-at-station.md (1:1 with the intent name)
Rules are illustrated by at least 3 Given/When/Then examples
Examples use concrete values (named actors, identifiers or numbers)
No solution vocabulary outside a technical-notes section
Every business-outcome event of the intent appears in the spec
Contract lists commands and events in domain language
Spec passes specs.py check (0 errors)
No plan, canvas, context map or code produced
15 minutes replaces the unknown duration (no '?' left for it)
Q1 and Q2 no longer open
Q2 answer reflected in rules/examples (rider must take exactly the reserved bike)
Spec status approved
